# tests/fixtures/

Test inputs and recorded/hand-crafted Codex/API responses for the snapshot test harness. Two architecturally distinct fixture corpora live here; future contributors should pick the right one and not blur the line.

## Two corpora, two purposes

| Corpus | Purpose | Source | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Recorded** (`api/{nasal_methylation,eif4enif1}/`, `codex/{nasal_methylation,eif4enif1}/`) | Lock real-Codex behaviour on real research documents. Catch regressions when Codex models update or `api_verify.py` semantics change. | Captured from one-time live runs of the orchestrator against the original docx files (which are NOT in the repo — they're the user's actual research). Timestamps and codex_model are normalized in the snapshot, but everything else is exactly what real Codex / Crossref / OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar returned. | When you want a sanity check that the integration with real external systems still produces sane outputs. Expensive to refresh (Codex quota, network); refresh deliberately. |
| **Hand-crafted** (`api/{synthetic_happy,synthetic_mixed}/`, `codex/{synthetic_happy,synthetic_mixed}/`) | Lock the orchestrator's *internal* logic (bucketing, correction assembly, replacement chain) against a deterministic, designed-by-us contract. | The synthetic docx files in `inputs/synthetic_*.docx` are generated by `tests/_make_synthetic_docx.py` (deterministic zip envelope). The accompanying api/codex fixtures are written by `tests/_build_synthetic_mixed_fixtures.py` from data tables that paste real Crossref records as canonical anchors and explicitly author Channel B / Stage 4 responses against the documented schemas. | When you want to verify an orchestrator change without touching real Codex. Re-running the builder regenerates byte-identical fixtures. JOSS reviewers running `pytest tests/` only ever exercise this corpus. |

The recorded corpus tells us "real Codex hasn't broken in some way we'd notice." The hand-crafted corpus tells us "the orchestrator's logic still does what we designed." Both are necessary; neither is sufficient.

## What lives where

```
tests/fixtures/
├── inputs/                              # synthetic docx files (committed)
│   ├── synthetic_happy.docx             # 3 valid Vancouver-numbered citations
│   └── synthetic_mixed.docx             # 6 citations covering all 4 Stage-4b buckets
├── api/<case>/                          # Channel A (api_verify.py) recorded stdout
│   └── citation_<id>_<sha8>.json        # keyed by citation_id + sha256(citation_json)[:8]
└── codex/<case>/                        # Codex atomic call recorded stdout
    ├── stage2_input.json                # atomize references (citations.schema.json)
    ├── stage3_input_<id>.json           # Channel B verify (verdict.schema.json)
    ├── stage3_input_<id>_reverify.json  # Stage 4 winner re-verify (verdict.schema.json)
    ├── stage4a_input_<id>.json          # find_alternatives (alternatives.schema.json)
    ├── stage4b_input_<id>_<rank>.json   # score_context_fit (fit_score.schema.json)
    └── stage4b_input_<id>.json          # build_correction (correction_diff.schema.json)
```

The api fixture filename's `_<sha8>` discriminator is needed because Stage 4's replacement-search re-verifies a winner candidate using the *same* `citation_id` but different content; without the hash, both calls collide on one fixture file.

Phase 2 fixtures (nasal_methylation, eif4enif1) predate the hash discriminator and are stored at the legacy path `citation_<id>.json`. The runner falls back to the legacy path in replay mode if no hash-suffixed file exists.

## Adding a new case

**If the new case is a real research document:** record fixtures via

    .venv/bin/python3 tests/_record_fixtures.py --case <name> --input <path-to-docx> --persist-snapshot

This consumes Codex quota and hits Channel A endpoints live. Run once, commit the captured fixtures, and don't refresh casually.

**If the new case is a synthetic stress-test:** extend `tests/_make_synthetic_docx.py` with a new scenario and `tests/_build_synthetic_mixed_fixtures.py` (or a sibling builder) with the corresponding hand-crafted api/codex fixtures. Then run the orchestrator in replay mode against the new fixtures and persist the resulting `corrections.json` / `verdicts.json` / `replacements.json` to `tests/snapshots/<case>/`.

In both cases:

- Add a `pytest.param` row to `CASES` in `tests/test_pipeline_snapshots.py`.
- Verify `tests/test_fixture_schema_parity.py` is happy with the new codex fixtures (it auto-discovers them).
- Update `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased] / Added` with a one-line entry.

## Why hand-crafted fixtures don't get re-recorded

A hand-crafted fixture's authority is the schema, not the live Codex. If the schema changes (new required field, type tightened, enum value added or removed), the parity test (`tests/test_fixture_schema_parity.py`) fails and the fixture must be updated by editing the builder. There is intentionally no automatic re-record path for synthetic fixtures — that would conflate "designed contract" with "captured behaviour" and reintroduce the flakiness the hand-crafted approach was meant to escape.
